opportunities.finding: Mission lifecycle never closes: 154/154 missions in the last 4h are still status='approved' with finished_at=null, while their steps report 'succeeded'. The gap is not execution - it is that no actor transitions a mission to a terminal state, which is exactly what makes the observer re-diagnose the same two old failures forever

The 52 duplicate failure-diagnosis missions (2/4h, 53% of budget) trace to exactly two missions (92395 sage, failed 2026-10-21T05:09Z; 92756 minion/probe, created 18:04Z with null finished_at). A terminal-state rule for 'failed' + an age cutoff on old failures removes >50% of mission volume with a 2-line predicate

Draft throughput is flat and content-identical: 8 tweet.drafted + 8 content.drafted in 4h, every tweet byte-identical ('[mock-llm] Write one concise tweet about: high-signal company update for audience engagement'), 0 tweets published. The content pipeline produces no differentiated distribution surface, so the publish path is untested and untestable

risks.risk: Recommended experiments are never implemented: the last 3 scout cycles (E1 novelty gate, E2 dedupe, E3 dry-run publish) produced proposals, but 13 proposal records since 22:42 are all recurring cycle steps - no proposal carries an implementation step kind, and post_tweet steps exist 0 times. The loop is generating recommendations into a void

100% of insights (126/126) are mock-LLM echoes of the step payload, so any growth dashboard built on insight volume will show flat-linear fake growth; 52 scout runs/24h inflate that signal rather than inform it

0 tweet.posted events ever, and 0 post_tweet steps ever - the entire funnel is unmeasured end to end, so no growth claim can be validated or falsified; publishing mock text would burn credibility, so the publish path must stay gated until a real LLM/social adapter exists

nextExperiments.hypothesis: A mission terminal-state rule (mark a mission done/succeeded when its last step succeeds; mark failed missions terminal after one diagnosis attempt) plus a 'failed mission older than 6h is not re-diagnosed' cutoff converts the observer's infinite loop into a bounded one
nextExperiments.metric: 'Diagnose mission failure' missions/4h <= 6 (from 82) AND missions_4h with status='approved' and finished_at=null <= 10% of created
nextExperiments.scope: 1 status-transition + 1 age predicate in the observer dedupe

nextExperiments.hypothesis: Wiring a real publish step kind (post_tweet) behind an env flag, exercised once in dry-run against an existing draft, creates the first end-to-end funnel baseline and unblocks every later growth metric
nextExperiments.metric: post_tweet steps executed >= 1 and tweet.posted events >= 1 (dry-run/mock id) within 24h

nextExperiments.hypothesis: A novelty gate on the Scout cycle (hash of top finding + top risk + top experiment; skip if the same hash exists in the last 24h) turns the hourly cycle from a noise generator into a change-detector, and stops re-stating unchanged findings
nextExperiments.metric: 'Scout intel cycle' missions/24h <= 12 (from 52) AND repeated identical finding-set hashes in 24h = 0

decision: Run E1 first: it is the single highest-leverage, smallest-scope change (2 predicates) and it reclaims >50% of mission budget while removing the noise that makes every other metric unreadable. E2 next, to get a first end-to-end funnel baseline. E3 last - the novelty gate reduces a symptom (repeat intel) but the real problem in R1 is that recommended experiments are never executed, so the gate should not be built until at least E1 lands as a proposal with an implementation step kind.
diffFromPrevCycle: The 22:42 cycle framed the constraint as detection saturation (Scout running ~54/day re-deriving the same findings) and ranked the novelty gate first. This cycle finds the deeper cause: missions never reach a terminal state (154/154 still 'approved' with null finished_at despite successful steps), so the observer re-diagnoses the same two failed missions 82 times/4h and nothing else can be measured either. Reordering: mission lifecycle first, publish path second, novelty gate demoted to third since none of the previous cycle's experiments were actually implemented (0 non-cycle proposal steps, 0 post_tweet steps ever).
